messages:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION triggered in eu-west-1 for service: inference-runtime. Severity: P1. TTL: 15m. @oncall-infra @oncall-sre

alice.nguyen: getting the page. seeing steady increase in queued requests + throttles on pool-gpu-eu-west1. CPU of control-plane fine, GPU utilization 98% across pool.

ben.ramirez: confirming — autoscaler tried 3 scale operations, all failed with "quota_limit_exceeded: cannot attach more GPUs to pool" from provider. queue length jumped from ~120 -> 820 in 8m.

cheng.li: any recent deploys? model routing?

alice.nguyen: yes, we rolled model v23.4 to canary route earlier (09:12 UTC). Telemetry shows median context length up ~3.7x for requests routed to v23.4 due to tokenizer change. Prefill times spiked.

dana_k: impact: multiple customers reporting 5xx and streaming disconnects. Metrics: p95 latency for generation increased from 220ms -> 2.8s for affected hosts, errors up 18%.

infra-oncall: hitting provider soft quota for GPUs on that account/region. I've opened an escalation ticket with partner (VM-CO-1842) but ETA unknown.

ben.ramirez: mitigation plan options:
- rollback model v23.4 to v23.3 on eu-west-1 routes (fastest).
- route traffic to eu-central cold pool (capacity) for impacted customers.
- enable aggressive kvcache eviction and reduce max_prefill_tokens to 512 temporarily.

cheng.li: rollbacks take ~2-4m per route and safe. Recommend rollback + kvcache eviction while infra escalates quota.

alice.nguyen: starting rollback to v23.3 on canary + scaling down v23.4 traffic now. Command: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --service inference-runtime --model v23.3 --region eu-west-1 --route canary`

prod-support-bot: Customer ticket 23456 created: high latency and 500s for model v23.4 in eu-west-1. Notified top-10 customers on the affected tenant list.

incident-bot: oncall handoff: @infra-oncall -> @sre-lead in 10m for escalation updates.

infra-oncall: also enabling temporary burstpool: `infractl pool update pool-gpu-eu-west1 --burst=true --burst-ttl=20m` (subject to quota check). Returning error: `quota_limit_exceeded`. burstpool blocked.

dana_k: logs from edge-proxy showing many prefill spikes. snippet:
```
WARN 09:17:34 prefill: token_count=8192 route=v23.4 request_id=abc123
ERROR 09:18:01 dispatch: queue_push_failed capacity=100 err=throttle_limit
```

ben.ramirez: kvcache: we can enable eviction policy experimental-evict-lru across v23.4 instances to free memory quickly: `confctl set inference.kvcache.eviction=evict-lru --scope region:eu-west-1`

cheng.li: do it. Also reduce prefill window at router: `routerctl set prefill.max_tokens=512 --region eu-west-1` — that will cap long prefill requests landing on GPUs.

alice.nguyen: applying kvcache eviction and router prefill cap now.

alice.nguyen: kvcache eviction applied. router prefill cap applied. seeing queue growth slow, but still high.

sre-lead: handoff: taking lead. @alice.nguyen keep rollback in-progress until we confirm p95 latency returning. @infra-oncall keep pushing provider ticket and ask for temporary quota bump.

infra-oncall: provider updated ticket: they can expedite if we shard onto a new project account or use spare capacity in another region. ETA if manual: ~25-40m.

dana_k: customer impact summary for leadership: ~14 tenants affected, partial degradations, no full tenant outages yet. RTO target: restore baseline latency within 30m.

ben.ramirez: quick note: v23.4 tokenizer change increases tokenization of certain UTF-8 sequences; real change in token count distribution for conversational traffic. That drove kvcache growth (more keys) and prefill amplification. We'll need a follow-up to add safe-routes for new models.

alice.nguyen: rollback completed for canary and 50% of traffic. Observed p95 dropping from 2.8s -> 340ms in 6m. queues: down 820 -> 130.

prod-support-bot: Updated tickets: customers alerted to partial mitigation, advising retry/backoff.

sre-lead: keep monitoring for 20m. Postmortem owners: @cheng.li (root cause), @ben.ramirez (post-deploy hardening), @alice.nguyen (mitigation timeline).

cheng.li: postmortem immediate items:
- revert tokenizer change in v23.4 until canary validates token distribution.
- add synthetic tests for token-length distribution on deploys.
- autoscaler: handle quota-failure path by routing to alternative region with fallback policy.

alice.nguyen: follow-up mitigations we did: rollback v23.4, set prefill cap, enabled kvcache eviction, asked provider for quota bump, created tickets for product owners.

infra-oncall: provider offered temporary cross-region burst: enabling routing of 25% of overflow to eu-central; applying now.

alice.nguyen: after shifting 25% overflow to eu-central, queue normalized to ~40, p95 at baseline ~230ms for most traffic.

sre-lead: incident status: mitigated. Still monitoring. Filing P1 -> Postmortem. Next steps: schedule postmortem doc, assign action items.

prod-support-bot: Notifying customers of mitigation and ETA for full recovery.

incident-bot: Incident status updated to M1 -> Postmortem requested.

alice.nguyen: thanks everyone. lessons learned: model-level token distribution changes can cascade into infra quota hits. Need deploy guardrails. :warning:

ben.ramirez: logging the deploy roll forward plan: once quota confirmed, re-evaluate v23.4 with tokenizer revert + smaller canary.

sre-lead: handoff complete. Closing active comms. If any regressions, reopen thread or ping #incidents immediately. :white_check_mark:
